definitions.explanation: Archaic and literary first-person pronoun, surviving in modern Japanese almost exclusively in fixed idioms. Refers to the self, especially one's own desires or will.

examples.japanese: {我|わ}を{忘|わす}れて{歌|うた}った。
{彼|かれ}はいつも{我|わ}を{張|は}って、{人|ひと}の{意見|いけん}を{聞|き}かない。
examples.english: He always insists on his own way and won't listen to other people's opinions.

notes:
Archaic first-person pronoun preserved in a small set of fixed expressions. Not used productively in modern Japanese — learners encounter it only in these idioms or in formal/literary writing.

FIXED EXPRESSIONS:
- {我|わ}を{通|とお}す: to have one's way; to insist on one's own view
- {我|わ}を{張|は}る: to be stubborn; to refuse to yield
- {我|わ}を{忘|わす}れる: to forget oneself; to lose oneself (in an activity or emotion)
- {我|わ}に{返|かえ}る: to come to one's senses

READINGS:
The same kanji {我} is also read われ (similarly archaic/literary, used as a stand-alone pronoun) and が (in compounds like {我儘|わがまま} selfish). The reading わ specifically appears in the idioms above.
